::: {#exr-zinf-moments}

Derive the [expected value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) and [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) of $Y$,
conditional on $\vX=\vx$ and $T=t$,
as functions of $\pi$ and $\mu_0$.
:::

::: {#sol-zinf-moments .solution}

**Expected value.**
By the [Law of Total Expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-conditional-lie)
(conditioning on $Z$, within the subpopulation $\{\vX=\vx, T=t\}$):

$$
\ba
\E{Y \mid \vX=\vx, T=t}
&= \pi \, \E{Y \mid Z=1, \vX=\vx, T=t} \\
&\phantom{={}} + (1-\pi) \, \E{Y \mid Z=0, \vX=\vx, T=t} \\
&\quad \text{(by Law of Total Expectation; } Z \ind T \mid \vX\text{)} \\
&= 0 \cdot \pi + \mu_0 (1-\pi) \\
&\quad \text{(substituting the conditional means)} \\
&= (1-\pi) \mu_0 \\
&\quad \text{(simplifying arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

The substitution $\E{Y \mid Z=0, \vX=\vx, T=t} = \mu_0$ follows immediately
from the definition of $\mu_0$.

**Variance.**
Within this derivation,
write $\E{\,\cdot \mid Z}$ and $\Var{\cdot \mid Z}$
for the moments conditional on $Z$ **and** on $\vX=\vx, T=t$;
the outer operators keep their conditioning explicit.
By the [Law of Total Variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-total-variance):

$$
\ba
\Var{Y \mid \vX=\vx, T=t}
&= \E{\Var{Y \mid Z} \mid \vX=\vx, T=t} \\
&\phantom{={}} + \Var{\E{Y \mid Z} \mid \vX=\vx, T=t} \\
&\quad \text{(by Law of Total Variance)}
\ea
$$

For the expected conditional variance term, note that

$$\Var{Y \mid Z=1} = 0 \quad\text{and}\quad \Var{Y \mid Z=0} = \mu_0$$

since the $Z=0$ arm is Poisson, so:

$$
\ba
\E{\Var{Y \mid Z} \mid \vX=\vx, T=t}
&= \pi \, \Var{Y \mid Z=1} + (1-\pi) \, \Var{Y \mid Z=0} \\
&\quad \text{(expectation over } Z\text{; } Z \ind T \mid \vX\text{)} \\
&= 0 \cdot \pi + \mu_0 (1-\pi) \\
&\quad \text{(substituting the conditional variances)} \\
&= (1-\pi)\mu_0 \\
&\quad \text{(simplifying arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

For the variance of conditional expectation term,
$\E{Y \mid Z}$ takes value 0 (with probability $\pi$)
or $\mu_0$ (with probability $1-\pi$), so:

$$
\ba
\Var{\E{Y \mid Z} \mid \vX=\vx, T=t}
&= \pi \paren{0 - (1-\pi)\mu_0}^2 + (1-\pi) \paren{\mu_0 - (1-\pi)\mu_0}^2 \\
&\quad \text{(variance over } Z\text{; } Z \ind T \mid \vX\text{)} \\
&= \pi(1-\pi)^2 \mu_0^2 + (1-\pi)\pi^2 \mu_0^2 \\
&\quad \text{(expanding squared terms)} \\
&= \pi(1-\pi)\mu_0^2 \sb{(1-\pi) + \pi} \\
&\quad \text{(factoring)} \\
&= \pi(1-\pi)\mu_0^2 \\
&\quad \text{(since } (1-\pi) + \pi = 1\text{)}
\ea
$$

Combining both terms gives:

$$
\ba
\Var{Y \mid \vX=\vx, T=t}
&= (1-\pi)\mu_0 + \pi(1-\pi)\mu_0^2 \\
&\quad \text{(summing expected variance and variance of expectation)} \\
&= (1-\pi)\mu_0 \paren{1 + \pi\mu_0} \\
&\quad \text{(factoring out } (1-\pi)\mu_0\text{)}
\ea
$$

The logistic model puts $\pi$ strictly between 0 and 1,
since $\expit$ never attains its limits,
and $\mu_0 = t \exp{\eta(\vx)} > 0$ whenever $t > 0$.
Then $1 + \pi\mu_0 > 1$, so

$$(1-\pi)\mu_0 (1+\pi\mu_0) > (1-\pi)\mu_0 = \E{Y \mid \vX=\vx, T=t}$$

and a zero-inflated count model is [overdispersed](#def-overdispersion)
relative to a Poisson model with the same mean,
at every covariate pattern with positive exposure.

:::
